subject: Urgent: FastLedger post-upgrade throughput spiral & 500s
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@fastledger.com>
To: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-11 09:22 PDT
Subject: Re: Upgrade this morning — service impact

Mina —

We just observed a sharp increase in 500s and end-to-end latency after you flipped the v4.2 -> v4.3 model bundle at 07:10 PT. Our dashboard shows p95 jumping from ~180ms to ~1.2s and p99 from ~300ms to ~2.7s. Throughput dropped as many requests retried; error rate for our batch endpoint is now ~6%. I attached a short log sample and a perf snapshot.

This is customer-critical — it’s affecting checkout flows for a handful of merchants. Can you confirm you rolled any quantization profiles or changed runtime kernels as part of the upgrade? We need an ETA for rollback or mitigations.

Thanks,
Sara Kim
VP Engineering, FastLedger

Attachments referenced: fastledger-500-sample.log, p99-trend-20250511.png
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-11 09:34 PDT
Subject: Re: Upgrade this morning — service impact

Sara — thank you for the heads up and the logs. I’m pulling the on-call infra/serving leads into this thread. Initial answers: we rolled v4.3 globally for your prod project at 07:07 PT and applied an updated quant-profile (qprofile-03) for throughput optimizations targeting float16 paths. No kernel changes beyond the runtime autopicker.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Marcus will validate if qprofile-03 is triggering slower decode paths for your sequence-length distribution.
- I’ll put a temporary traffic split to keep 20% on v4.2 while we triage (should reduce error surface).
- If impact persists we will stage a rollback to v4.2 and restore qprofile-02.

Ben — can you loop in the account team for an exec update so FastLedger has a single point of contact?

Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Quick data requests while Marcus digs in:
1) Marcus — pull a per-CPU/GPU timeline for the affected nodes from 06:50–09:00 PT (batch sizes + queue times). I want to see if quantization induced more kernel thrashing or additional memcpy overhead.
2) Mina — can we get a one-line summary of what changed between qprofile-02 and qprofile-03 (quant scales, fallback thresholds)? I don’t want to assume it’s only numeric scales; sometimes the qprofile will flip operator implementations.
3) Ben — prep a short customer-facing note: what we’re doing and expected ETA for rollback if needed. Keep it high level.

I’ll stand by to approve rollback if Marcus finds regressions tied to the qprofile.

— Karthik

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-05-11 11:18 PDT
Subject: Re: Upgrade this morning — service impact

Investigations so far (prelim):
- Replayed a sampled request set from FastLedger between 07:05–07:15 PT on canary infra. v4.3 + qprofile-03 shows 2.2–3.1x higher token-decode time for sequences where tokens per request > 120. Firewall of evidence: trace IDs and flame samples attached to internal S3 (link in notes).
- The qprofile-03 changes include: narrower per-channel scale clipping and an aggressive INT8 fallback for certain matmul sizes; appears to hit a slow reference kernel for the rare matmul shapes FastLedger emits.
- Kernel selection logs show a fallback to reference GEMM on Turing-class GPUs for a subset of batches — this explains the p99 spike and the throughput collapse. Not a runtime memory issue.

Immediate mitigation ops we ran:
- Rolled a partial traffic split (20% to v4.2) at 09:00 PT — customer p99 improved by ~35% in the 09:05–09:20 window.
- Disabled the INT8 aggressive fallback for FastLedger project (hotfix flag: disable-int8-fallback=true). That reduced the reference kernel occurrence on replay.

Suggested next steps:
- If customer approves, full rollback of qprofile to qprofile-02 (expected 15–25 min to complete and validate).
- Postmortem: adjust qprofile autopicker to consider observed matmul shape distribution for FastLedger-like workloads; add a guard to prevent fallback to reference kernels for hot paths.

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: RE: Upgrade this morning — service impact (executive summary & next steps)

Sara / Michael —

Thanks again for flagging this. Short executive summary and next actions from Redwood: 

What happened (short):
- During the 07:07 PT v4.3 model swap we also promoted qprofile-03 which contains an aggressive INT8 fallback path. For FastLedger’s typical token lengths this triggered a reference GEMM kernel on several batches; that single-path regression caused p95/p99 spikes and higher 500s as queueing cascaded.

What we did (actions taken 05/11–05/12):
- Put a 20% traffic split back to v4.2 at 09:00 PT to reduce exposure.
- Temporarily disabled the INT8 fallback flag for your project (hotfix).
- Per-customer rollback plan ready: we can revert qprofile to qprofile-02 across your prod fleet; estimated impact window 15–25 minutes plus validation (we will run a small canary first).

Immediate options for you:
1) Authorize rollback to qprofile-02 now (recommended if you prefer conservative stability).
2) Allow Redwood to proceed with a targeted qprofile tweak that preserves most v4.3 improvements but prevents GEMM fallback for your hot shapes (we'd need ~4–8 hours to QA).

Executive support: Ben will set up a 1:1 with your leadership for a status update; Karthik and Marcus are available for a technical review. We will prepare a short postmortem within 48 hours and a compensation credit proposal for the disruption.

Proposed immediate next step: a 30-minute bridge at 16:00 PT today to agree rollback vs tweak and confirm SLAs. If you’d like us to start the rollback immediately we can do so on approval.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re treating this as an exec priority until resolved.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
